chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Intentional killing is when someone deliberately targets a thing and strikes it with an iron object, or with a stone, or with a stick, or with a thrust; all of that is intentional. Mistake is when someone intends a thing but strikes someone else.”

key_terms.اعْتَمَدَ: intended or deliberately directed oneself toward a target
key_terms.الْخَطَأُ: mistaken or accidental action in legal context
key_terms.الْعَمْدَ: intentional action or deliberate harm in legal context
key_terms.بِحَدِيدَةٍ: with an iron instrument or metal weapon
key_terms.بِوَكْزَةٍ: with a thrust, jab, or forceful blow
key_terms.غَيْرَهُ: someone other than the intended target

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام distinguish between intentional and mistaken killing in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the legal distinction between intentional harm and mistaken harm in cases relevant to diyat and qisas. It explains that deliberate striking with lethal or harmful means constitutes intentional action, while error occurs when one aims at one target but hits another.
